source_findings.finding: DisplayRefreshQuery comment says Windows only, nullopt elsewhere. HostPacer depends refresh-known and VK_KHR_present_wait; cannot directly assume Linux/Sway active.

PresentWait thread with 4ms waits and 500ms deadline, rendered-frame wait, learned display grid; <=30fps avoids long hold and feeds g_host_phase_ns back to service. Needs lifecycle/mutex/extension/Wayland review, no port yet.

Own oot_30fps forces effective swap interval>=2; dynamic time-step assumption. Genlock adjusts service interval within1% display refresh; can change speed slightly, not accepted blindly. Has legacy600/599 pacing-stat bias still present.
Existing Scheduler Wait algorithm broadly same as our frozen base; new host pacing is elsewhere, not automatically a fix for our Wait.

Confirmed source lines105–168 DisplayRefreshQuery::Query returns nullopt outside _WIN32; Refresh179–202 requires refresh_known to enable pacing. Header comments confirmed in actual implementation. Direct import would leave this pacer off on Linux, even if VK_KHR_present_wait is supported.

Genlock shifts pacing deadline and phase, with <=1% interval adjustment; aligns30fps to refresh via g_host_phase_ns; not a mere Scheduler Wait replacement. Would require explicit Linux presentation timing and speed/latency validation before any port.

next: Prioritize ongoing continuous ground-motion and AV qualifications. If actual first-visit stalls remain, inspect compatible preparation/key normalization. Review ASTC bounds as a separate correctness candidate. No whole-fork rebase or Windows executable deployment.

base_source_comparison: ASTC decode guards only the block origin; direct image stores and unswizzle stores lack the per-store upper-bound checks in f52631cf. No local out-of-range write or associated corruption reproduced.

Our base lacks the relocation and render-frame-clock machinery. The render-frame counter in e722284e tracks resource-cache frame boundaries, not simulation time; its source is later changed in the release, so do not import this isolated predecessor as the finished design.
The AMD precompile-key conversion targets NVIDIA-recorded recipes and static logic-op state. No proof our RADV driver has that feature mismatch or that a prepared recipe matches our cache format.
The address relocation guard depends on the new relocation machinery; it is not a standalone speed patch for our base.
